claims.text: All four vendors document backing up Hyper-V VMs (uncited)
AWS Backup supports Hyper-V as a workload and integrates with Hyper-V platform [1][2]
AWS Backup supports backing up VMs managed by a hypervisor [3]
FortKnox supports archival, recovery, clone, cancel, file recovery workflows for HyperV 2016/2019 and 2012R2 [4][5]
FortKnox Cloud Vault from which Hyper-V VMs can be recovered, to original or new location [6][7]
FortKnox instant volume mount with Hyper-V VM as target [8]
FortKnox supports workflows for ESXi, vCloud Director, Hyper-V, Acropolis [9]
Azure Backup backs up on-prem Hyper-V VMs using DPM or MABS agent [10]
MABS backs up Hyper-V VMs [11][12]
VBR supports/creates backups of Hyper-V VMs [13][14]
Documented for AWS
Documented for Cohesity
Documented for Microsoft
Documented for Veeam

A.notes: Claims AWS documents Hyper-V backup, but [1] and [2] say nothing about Hyper-V.

claims.text: Only two vendors document backing up Hyper-V VMs (uncited)
VBR supports Hyper-V: platform versions, VM requirements, infrastructure components, creating Hyper-V backup jobs [1][4][8][9][10]
MABS can back up Hyper-V VMs, with supported scenarios, prerequisites, protection matrix [2][3][5][6]

B.notes: Silent on AWS and omits Cohesity (FortKnox supports Hyper-V); uncited claim that only two vendors document it.

claims.text: Only two products support shipping initial backup data on physical devices (uncited)
Azure Backup offline seeding copies initial full backup to physical devices shipped to Azure datacenter and uploaded to Recovery Services vault [1]
VBR can use AWS Snowball Edge to transport data instead of full backup over internet [2]
VBR allows a removable storage device to ship backups to the DR site for seeding [3]

A.notes: Silent on AWS and Cohesity (no-evidence facts absent).

claims.text: AWS Snowball Edge is a physical device emulating a cloud storage endpoint between local repository and S3; avoids full backup over internet [1]
Order device, connect, copy backups, ship back; then initial sync with S3 [1]
Add as AWS Snowball Edge Storage, then standalone object storage repo or capacity/performance tier of SOBR, offload data [1][2]
Put object storage repo in Maintenance mode, power off, ship back to AWS [1]
Synchronize seeded data with S3 account [1]
Offloading to Snowball Edge much faster than direct transfer to Amazon object storage [2]
As capacity extent, select 'Copy backups to object storage as soon as they are created' to keep local copy during shipment [1][7]
Sources describe no other physical seeding products besides Snowball Edge (uncited)

B.notes: Describes Veeam's Snowball Edge seeding but never attributes it to Veeam/VBR; omits Azure offline seeding; silent on AWS/Cohesity no-evidence.
